headline: Margin gains offset by one-time charges, profit dips
summary_short: Colgate-Palmolive posted Q2 FY2026 net sales of $5.36B, up 4.9% y/y (organic sales +2.4%), with GAAP EPS down 5% to $0.86 on restructuring charges while Base Business (non-GAAP) EPS rose 8% to $0.99.
summary_long: Net sales rose 4.9% y/y to $5.36B (organic sales +2.4%), led by Latin America (+13.7% reported, +8.4% FX tailwind) and Asia Pacific (+4.9%), while North America declined 3.0% on a 3.9% organic volume drop. GAAP gross margin expanded 140bp to 61.5%. GAAP operating profit fell 6% to $1.016B and GAAP EPS fell 5% to $0.86, both pressured by $129M of Strategic Growth and Productivity Program charges; Base Business (non-GAAP) operating profit rose 5% to $1.145B and non-GAAP EPS rose 8% to $0.99. Cash stood at $1.37B against $7.82B long-term debt. Colgate reaffirmed FY2026 net sales growth guidance of 2%-6% and organic sales growth of 1%-4%.

drivers.explanation: Growth was led by Latin America (+13.7% reported, +8.4% FX tailwind) and Asia Pacific (+4.9%), partly offset by North America (-3.0%) on a 3.9% organic volume decline.
The 140bp y/y gross margin gain to 61.5% is not explained in the release beyond the headline figure.
GAAP operating profit fell 6% on $129M of Strategic Growth and Productivity Program restructuring charges booked in Corporate; Base Business (ex-charges) operating profit rose 5%.
GAAP diluted EPS fell 5% on the same $129M Strategic Growth and Productivity Program charges (a $0.13/share drag); Base Business EPS rose 8% to $0.99 excluding them.
Management cited broad-based top- and bottom-line growth, organic volume improving for a third straight quarter, and a 15% increase in advertising spend behind the 2030 growth strategy.
